title: Louis and Lil Armstrong, and who wrote the tunes
summary: He discusses Lil's lasting feelings for Louis, her death, her claim on the tune credits, and Jelly Roll Morton's recordings.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Yeah. And she fell off the pen and dead and heart attack. So I attribute that to her grieving. She never forget him. And I did have a little hassle on her. This tune strutting with some barbecue. I understand she said it was his and she said it was hers. Well you know Lil was a very good musician. You see she graduated from some college down in Tennessee. I don't know if it was Fisk or what anyhow. She even went with her job. And she used to get together in the head, we call that head you know. They'd get together and one would make a few notes, another would make a few notes and look around and they had a tune. All those tunes like dip them out and things like that, Canal Street Blues, they were right on the stand doing working hours you know. They'd get together and Lil would, as they played, Lil could write music you know. And so anyhow she got, she supposed to get $6,000 out of that. And now during this time we had Jellie Roermorten. Now Jellie was a card. You know he had this diamond in his teeth. And Jellie played with the New Harlem Rhythm Kings for a while. And he did a lot of recording around in Chicago. He had O'Reilly and Lil' George Mitchell on the carnet. And he had Andrew Hilliard who was from New Orleans too. One of the finalists on all the country you know. And we had, of course in this band was Jimmy Noon, Rob Palmer, Freddie Kepa. And I just said now let's talk about Freddie. Freddie didn't read so well but he never forgot when he got it tuned down. He played it down once or twice and he had it and that's it. And Coach Freddie was one of the strongest I ever heard. He really blasted. He was a large man and so was Joe Oliver. And so this Harmon's dreaming. The elevator ran right, the tracks was right over the top of it. And they needed a big band like that in order for the people to hear the band. And so it's a 26 piece band. But when Freddie started to blow in, they really heard it.
